question: does minimising Expected Free Energy select probes better than greedy, on a channel calibrated to the MEASURED single-look accuracy?
blueprint_clause: HENRI-ARCH-2026-SYSTEMIC-EVALUATION-V3 sec 1.4 / Stage 6: 'it lacks a recursive active inference loop to execute step-by-step state manipulation ... minimising Expected Free Energy G across candidate options pi'
labelling: DERIVED, NOT OBSERVED. Gaussian likelihood over the REAL codec waves (the 6 archived corpus facts, real encode_egress output), with the noise scale calibrated per rung. No physical claim. This tests the DECISION RULE.

policies.info: expected information gain (entropy of the look-ahead posterior)

verdict: EFE_SEPARATES_FROM_GREEDY at single-look acc 0.45 (info 2.0 vs greedy 3.0 probes, 0.67x)

THE_HONEST_READING.at_the_measured_operating_point: NO separation. At the system's measured single-look accuracy (0.8043) and at every rung >= 0.55, info does NOT beat greedy (G-AI-1 FAIL): info 1.0 vs greedy 1.0 at 0.80; 2.0 vs 2.0 at 0.65 and 0.55.
THE_HONEST_READING.where_separation_appears: only at rung 0.45, where the channel is calibrated to be much NOISIER than the real system. That rung is a derived counterfactual, not the system's operating regime.
THE_HONEST_READING.so: the blueprint's Stage 6 decision rule is NOT shown to help at the operating point the system actually measures. It helps only in a derived noisier regime. Claiming 'Stage 6 validated' from this would overstate the result.
THE_HONEST_READING.what_DOES_hold_at_every_rung: info beats RANDOM on mean probes at all 5 rungs (G-AI-4 PASS): 1.45 vs 1.67, 1.57 vs 2.25, 2.00 vs 2.90, 2.51 vs 4.22, 4.57 vs 7.58. Expected-information selection is a real information-seeking policy; it is simply not better than the greedy rule here.
THE_HONEST_READING.why_greedy_may_be_competitive: with K=6 the expected-top-1 posterior criterion and the entropy criterion often agree on which probe to pick; and the criterion reaches 0.95 in few looks. A larger K or a stricter criterion could separate them. That is a stated hypothesis, not measured.

gates.G-AI-2_rand_median_gt_greedy: PASS at 4 of 5 rungs (fails at 0.65 where both are 2.0)
gates.G-AI-3_calibration_rand_acc1: PASS at ALL 5 rungs after D35

self_caught_instrument_defects.D31: RETRACTED false defect. I claimed abs(mean) understated ambiguity; measured signed mean 0.181986 == abs mean 0.181986. All off-diagonal cosines are positive (0.0902..0.3156) because the codec fills empty rows with hash(text)-derived +1.0 slots, so nothing cancels. The original value was correct and my 'fix' was a no-op. Kept the abs() form as the right general definition.
self_caught_instrument_defects.D32: design defect: at the measured accuracy the task SATURATED (every policy <=2 looks, acc@2=1.0000) so the control could not lose. Fixed with the accuracy ladder.
self_caught_instrument_defects.D33: calibrated sigma on ONE direction, evaluated on N_PROBES different ones; single-look accuracy is direction-dependent (acc@1 0.8250 vs 0.80; 0.5250 vs 0.40). Fixed by averaging over directions.
self_caught_instrument_defects.D34: checked INFO's acc@1 against the rung target, but info and greedy CHOOSE better-than-average directions and must exceed an average-direction calibration (rung 0.80: info 0.8500, rand 0.7667). Calibration was correct; the gate measured policy quality. Fixed to judge calibration on rand and made the selection advantage its own gate (G-AI-4).
self_caught_instrument_defects.D35: calibration and evaluation drew DIFFERENT direction sets, so realized accuracy drifted past the gate at 2 of 5 rungs (0.6100 vs 0.55; 0.5200 vs 0.45) while 3 matched exactly. Fixed by calibrating on the SAME directions the run evaluates. Result: G-AI-3 PASS at all 5 rungs.
self_caught_instrument_defects.D36: display defect: the summary printed 'rungs where the control could lose' from the list that actually holds rungs where the control could NOT lose. Inverted label; the verdict branch was correct. Fixed to print both lists explicitly.

honest_limits: DERIVED: the channel is a calibrated Gaussian likelihood over real waves, not a physical measurement
K=6; the blueprint's typed manifolds are up to K=512
the separating rung (0.45) does not correspond to the system's measured operating accuracy (0.8043)
single seed; 400 trials per rung (median granularity 1 probe)
this is a DECISION-RULE result and says nothing about wave->text egress
